Subject: Data minimization & retention cutover — questions for regulated deployment

Hi Markus,

Thanks for hopping on this. Our compliance team is finalizing the cutover plan for the MedSys deployment and we need concrete answers on retention limits and redaction options for PII/PHI. Key asks: 

- What minimum retention floors can we enforce per-tenant (we need the ability to set a 0/30/90/365 day window)?
- For PHI fields (SSNs, MRNs, clinical notes), what redaction techniques do you support at ingestion vs. on-demand (field-level masks, entity-based removal, pseudonymization, token-vault reversible IDs)?
- How do your caching and KV layers behave on deletion requests — is there a TTL/flush window? Any risk of rehydration from warm cache?
- What artifacts can you provide as evidence of deletion (audit log entries, manifest of deleted object keys, signed timestamps)?
- Any known impact on model quality for the different approaches (hard delete vs. tokenization vs. NER-based scrub)?

We have a compliance audit on Oct 15 and need to pick a path and test it in a staging cutover next week. Can you send a short set of recommended configurations and the expected timeline for a tenant-level purge? Attaching our current retention table for reference.

Thanks,

Ava Bianco
Director, Product Compliance
MedSys Health

Attachment: medsys-retention-reference.csv
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Bianco <ava@medsys-health.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data minimization & retention cutover — questions for regulated deployment

Hi Ava — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Priyom (applied ML / infra) for the technical rundown. High-level answers below; I’ll follow up with an implementation sketch by EOD.

1) Per-tenant retention windows: supported. We expose tenant-level retention as a configuration flag (retain_days) and a scoped override. Typical safe floors we operate with are 0/30/90/365; we can also support custom values down to 0. For very short windows (0–7 days) there are operational trade-offs on cache churn and cold-start latency.

2) Redaction approaches we support:
   - Ingestion-time field-level masks (regex & NER): removes or replaces tokens before they enter storage. Fast and removes PHI upstream.
   - Pseudonymization with reversible vault: replaces identifiers with deterministic tokens and stores mapping in a tenant-scoped vault (HSM/KMS-backed). Good for case re-identification by legal.
   - One-way tokenization / hashing for non-reversible masking (recommended when re-ID is not needed).
   - Model input sanitization (client-side) + server-side fallback.

3) Cache behaviour: we have a KV cache layer and a serving prefix cache. Deletion request triggers a purge signal; immediate invalidation requests will mark keys stale, but physical eviction can take up to the next compaction window (default 15 minutes). For strict cutovers we can schedule a cache compaction job and a forced TTL=0 flush.

4) Deletion evidence: we emit a deletion manifest (S3 object keys with a signed timestamp), an audit log entry per object id, and a job run record (job id + hash). We can also provide an exported CSV for legal.

5) Quality impact: field-level removal on sensitive clinical notes may slightly reduce LLM recall for cases that rely on identifiers as anchors; pseudonymization preserves structure with minimal quality loss. We’ll include empirical delta estimates based on your sample set.

Priyom — can you add specifics about the purge job, KV compaction, and the reversible vault options? Once we align, I’ll propose a 3-step cutover MOP for MedSys.

—Markus
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Ava Bianco <ava@medsys-health.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data minimization & retention cutover — questions for regulated deployment

Hi all — quick technical notes and recommended defaults based on similar regulated customers. I kept the answers actionable so your engineers can test in staging quickly.

A. Purge & retention mechanics
- Tenant-level "retain_days" drives three things: object lifecycle policy on S3, metadata visibility (search index TTL), and KV cache TTL.
- Purge job: a scheduled batch that enumerates tenant object ids older than retain_days, marks them as deleted in metadata, enqueues delete work, and writes a deletion_manifest_<jobid>.json to the tenant evidence bucket. Typical run time depends on object count; we parallelize by shard.
- Forced cutover: run purge job, then run KV compaction with TTL=0 and a cache-flush signal. We also run a cold-start cycle to re-warm benign context caches (non-PHI).

B. Redaction options (implementation patterns)
1) Ingestion NER + mask pipeline (low operational complexity)
   - Pros: removes PHI before storage, no special vault required.
   - Cons: NER misses (~1–3% for messy notes) and residual tokens may remain; we recommend a second-pass regex scrub for known identifier patterns.

2) Pseudonymization with reversible mapping (tenant-scoped vault)
   - Pros: full re-ID path, minimal model quality impact.
   - Cons: Requires secure mapping storage (we use tenant-scoped KMS-wrapped vault), additional audit requirements and monthly key rotations.

3) Deterministic hashing (non-reversible)
   - Pros: simple, efficient, deterministic for joins.
   - Cons: irreversible; cannot satisfy legal re-ID requests.

4) Hybrid: hash sensitive identifiers + keep encrypted ancillary mapping for a short retention window (e.g., 90 days) — gives a middle ground.

C. Evidence and audit readiness
- Deletion manifest includes: object_key, last_modified, deleted_at (rfc3339), deletion_job_id. Manifests are signed with our system key and placed in the tenant evidence bucket with ACL restricted to the tenant's compliance role.
- Audit logs available for 1 year by default; extended retention is an add-on.

D. Example API flags / config snippets (staging):
- PUT /tenants/{id}/config {"retain_days":90, "redaction_mode":"pseudonymize", "vault":"tenant-hsm-01"} 
- POST /tenants/{id}/purge?force=true  --> returns {"job_id":"purge-20260908-01"}
- GET /evidence/{job_id}/manifest --> S3 presigned URL

E. Timeline estimate for a mid-size payer (40M rows, 1TB blob):
- Staging test (sample): 2 business days
- Full purge dry-run: 3–5 business days
- Forced cutover and verification: 1 business day

Attachments: redaction_matrix_v2.xlsx (decision matrix), s3-preservation-diagram.png (evidence flow).

If you want, we can spin up a staging tenant with these flags and run a demo purge against a snapshot.

—Priyom Das
Applied ML / Platform
Redwood Inference
